Start hereThis is a map of one person's computer, with an AI helper for each job drawn as a pet. Read it from the middle out:
  1. The middle is what Astra built and trusts most: The Farm, the Friendly Farmer who looks after the pets, the pets, and the programs she made.
  2. The glass sphere is the fence. Everything inside it (🐾) an AI may change; everything outside it may only be used.
  3. Outside the glass, trusted less as you go: the AI models, programs made by others, the devices, and Astra (L4), who says yes to every change.
  4. Lines show what flows between things. Click a ring below, or anything on the map, to see who may read, write or run it.
Architecture overviewA trust-zone diagram of a single-owner AI-agent platform on Windows: one LLM agent per domain, an orchestrator that installs and supervises them, and a human owner who approves every change. Read it from the centre out:
  1. Rings 0 to 3 sit inside the trust boundary: the trusted core, the orchestrator, the agents and the first-party code they may modify.
  2. The glass sphere is the trust boundary (the agent harness). Outside it: LLM providers, third-party software and services (supply chain), endpoints, and the owner.
  3. Rings are logical trust zones, not CPU protection rings, and grant nothing. Permissions are grants (R W X, least privilege) at privilege levels L1 to L4: L1 deterministic tools, L2 the app and its skills, L3 an LLM agent session, L4 the human approver.
  4. Each grant is marked ✓ In code (a technical control, with its proof), ⚠︎ Rule only (policy, nothing enforces it) or ○ Not built. Edges are data flows. Click any ring or node for its grants.

Every pet, program, AI model and device, on the ring where it lives. The glass is the agent harness: 🐾 everything inside it is an animal. Claude Code and Codex are rings around their AI. Switch between 2D and 3D at the bottom, and DEV for the standard engineering names. In 2D drag to move; in 3D drag to turn. Pinch to zoom. Click anything to see who may read, write or run it, and what flows to it.

Rings: where things liveTrust zones (rings), centre out

Inside out, each ring a sphere. A ring says where a thing lives; it grants nothing. Click a ring to light it up and see the grants that reach it.

Most trusted at the centre. A zone says where a component runs and who wrote it; it grants nothing. Click a zone to highlight it and list the permission grants that reach it. The small line under each name is the standard term.

L1 to L4: what each should be, and whether it is in codePrivilege levels L1 to L4: designed permissions vs enforced controls

R W X lives on grants, not on rings (Astra, 2026-10-17). Every card shows the four levels down the left: what each should be (its R W X on that thing), then whether that is in code (Astra, 2026-10-19). Click a level to see the grants behind it, and the proof of every In code.

L1a pet's programs and tools: they act with their pet's grants, never more
L2a pet program and its runtime
L3an AI agent in a seat (Claude Code, Codex, or a pet's own agent)
L4you, the verified human who owns the farm
RWXread, write, run: yes
Wonly on a branch, merged after Astra's OK in chat
Ronly with a grant that Astra approves
Xonly after the harness asks Astra
Wno
✓ In codea test, setting or script makes it true, and names its proof
⚠︎ Rule onlya rule agents follow; nothing stops a break
○ Not builtdesigned, not built yet

Moving around

Left-drag or scroll-click drag turns the map freely; Shift + scroll-click drag pans. Scroll zooms toward the centre, or toward what you selected. Right-drag looks around; while holding it, W A S D fly, Q/E down and up, Shift faster. F frames what you selected. Esc closes the card. On a phone: one finger turns, two fingers zoom and pan.
